title: Modulators, mixers and detectors
blurb: Explain how FM, SSB and mixing signals are produced and detected, and why pre-emphasis and de-emphasis are used.

E7E01.why: Frequency is changed at the oscillator, so use **reactance modulation of a local oscillator**.
E7E01.trap: Balanced modulation cancels a carrier (DSB and SSB). It doesn't vary frequency.

E7E02.why: Varying a **capacitance** (reactance) in the oscillator makes its frequency or phase follow the audio: **PM or FM**.
E7E02.trap: Varying a resistance or inductance isn't how a reactance modulator works, and AM isn't its product.

E7E03.why: A **frequency discriminator** turns frequency variations back into audio: it **detects FM**.
E7E03.trap: FM generators are modulators, not discriminators.

E7E04.why: A balanced modulator cancels the carrier, then a **filter** removes one sideband: SSB.
E7E04.trap: A product detector demodulates; it doesn't make a transmit signal.

E7E05.why: A **pre-emphasis** network boosts the high audio frequencies before modulation.
E7E05.trap: De-emphasis is the receiver's matching cut.

E7E06.why: A phase modulator already tilts the audio toward the highs. De-emphasis flattens it, giving **compatibility with phase-modulated transmitters**.

E7E07.why: **Baseband** is the frequency range occupied by the message signal **before modulation**.
E7E07.trap: It is not the lowest band the radio covers.

E7E08.why: A mixer outputs **both inputs plus their sum and difference**, such as 14, 9, 23 and 5 MHz.
E7E08.trap: Harmonics and square roots aren't the mixer's main outputs.

E7E09.why: Excess input drive overloads the mixer's non-linear action, creating **spurious mixer products**.

E7E10.why: The diode **rectifies** the RF (one half-cycle only), then a capacitor **filters** off the RF, leaving the audio envelope.
E7E10.trap: Zener breakdown and reactance sensing aren't how an envelope detector works.

E7E11.why: SSB has no carrier, so a **product detector** (a mixer with a local oscillator) restores the audio.
E7E11.trap: Discriminators and phase detectors are FM and PLL circuits.
